population.span: In this double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 8442 patients with class II, III, or IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less

endpoint.span: The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for heart failure

estimate.span: At the time of study closure, the primary outcome had occurred in 914 patients (21.8%) in the LCZ696 group and 1117 patients (26.5%) in the enalapril group (hazard ratio in the LCZ696 group, 0.80; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.87; P<0.001).

ci.span: At the time of study closure, the primary outcome had occurred in 914 patients (21.8%) in the LCZ696 group and 1117 patients (26.5%) in the enalapril group (hazard ratio in the LCZ696 group, 0.80; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.87; P<0.001).

analysis_set.span: Full Analysis Set (FAS) included all randomized patients but the following two exclusions: 6 patients who did not qualify for randomization but were inadvertently randomized into the study and did not receive double-blind study medication; 37 patients because they were randomized at sites that were closed due to serious GCP violations

treatment_strategy.span: to receive either LCZ696 (at a dose of 200 mg twice daily) or enalapril (at a dose of 10 mg twice daily), in addition to recommended therapy.

follow_up.span: The trial was stopped early, according to prespecified rules, after a median follow-up of 27 months, because the boundary for an overwhelming benefit with LCZ696 had been crossed.

served_mismatch: The served HR and confidence interval match the abstract. The served analysis_set label 'intention-to-treat' lacks the registry's qualification: the primary outcome uses FAS with two exclusions from the randomized population. The claimed fulltext_verified provenance cannot be established from this packet, which holds abstracts and a registry record.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The entry criteria specify adults with NYHA class II-IV heart failure and reduced ejection fraction; the FAS exclusions are a separate analysis-set qualification.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Outpatients ≥ 18 years of age, male or female. * Patients with a diagnosis of CHF NYHA class II-IV and reduced ejection fraction (EF =\< 35%) and elevated BNP.

notes: Registry evidence supplies the analysis-set definition and adult eligibility. The FAS definition is repeated verbatim for several registry outcomes, including the primary composite. No full text is held. The abstract reports an ejection-fraction threshold of 40% or less, whereas registry eligibility states 35% or less; both describe HFrEF.
